author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: A single-page piece from the Berkeley Daily Gazette (August 14, 1944), written in Dick's mid-teens—early apprentice work whose title later gathers resonance against his 1974 visionary experiences recorded in the Exegesis.
page_summary:
The Visitation is a short item Dick published in the Berkeley Daily Gazette on August 14, 1944, when he was about fifteen. It survives as a one-page scan and sits among the juvenilia he wrote as a teenage contributor to the local paper, part of the same childhood apprenticeship as his other Gazette pieces.

As an early work its value is biographical: it marks Dick writing and appearing in print through his adolescence, well before the professional career of the 1950s. The piece itself is too brief to carry the developed concerns of his later fiction and is best read as an early exercise.

The title, however, acquires an accidental resonance in light of what came later. The archive links this record to Dick's 1974 visionary episodes—the dreams, voices, and sense of a 'Real Presence' documented in the Exegesis—so that a teenager's word for a supernatural arrival stands, decades early, over the events that would consume the end of his life. The connection is thematic and retrospective, not something present in the 1944 text.

biography_events.event: Dream of "Paul" holding up prophetic galleyproofs with Phil's name in them.
Hearing the "Voice" confirm that the Savior is born (The Park).
Observation of "Real Presence" on the faces of animals (Pinky/Ralph).
Realization that his "14 months of research" established the reality of the Ultimate.
